title: Deterministic Verification with a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We conducted a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the identical LLM-generated candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics). For N = 250 intents we generated one initial candidate per intent with gpt-5-mini and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated, template-driven repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial generations + 1 repair). Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. The preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed; the reported confirmatory estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition that was run. We archive all execution and analysis artifacts referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) promise to simplify operator intent→device configuration workflows but introduce operational risk: syntactic errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or nonfunctional device changes. A pragmatic architectural response is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that accepts only candidates that pass a deterministic validator and optionally applies bounded automated repairs when mechanically verifiable defects are detected. Prior surveys and empirical work document LLM feasibility for draft configurations while stressing the continuing need for deterministic verification or human oversight [1],[2].

This study asks a narrowly scoped, confirmatory question under preregistration: when the same initial model candidate is reused for both conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics), how large is the marginal verifier-detected improvement from inserting a deterministic validator plus allowing a single automated repair? The design isolates only validator-and-repair effects on identical model outputs and therefore does not measure effects of constrained prompting, model re-generation, or alternative first-pass prompts. Our primary contribution is an artifact-backed quantification of that marginal effect for a constrained NetOps task bank (N_pairs = 250) executed on a synthetic/emulation partition with gpt-5-mini.
sections.related_work:
Three empirical and conceptual strands motivate this work. First, multiple recent studies and surveys show that LLMs can produce usable draft configurations in controlled environments, but they also report residual syntax/semantic errors that warrant verification [1],[2],[3]. Second, deterministic network verification tools and formal-analysis approaches (e.g., header-space/Plankton, Batfish-style evolutions) are mature techniques for checking forwarding, reachability, and local-policy properties and are commonly used as validators in GVR pipelines [4],[5]. Third, generate-and-verify and program-repair workflows in code and configuration domains demonstrate that deterministic checks plus bounded repairs reduce mechanically verifiable defects, though deep semantic correctness and cross-vendor behaviors remain challenging [6],[7].

Security analyses of prompt-injection emphasize that retrieval/tooling chains and LLM-integrated applications require defensive layers (filtering, validators) but note adaptive adversaries remain an unresolved threat; our confirmatory run did not exercise adversarial attacks [8]. This study differs by using a sealed preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics to isolate the marginal validator/repair effect on identical candidates and by archiving complete validator traces and deterministic reconciliation artifacts for auditability.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 and froze a confirmatory paired design with N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, a single automated repair permitted per episode, exclusion/contamination rules, and analysis procedures (exact McNemar two-sided and paired-bootstrap percentile CIs). The preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the evidence bundle and reported in the Disclosure Statement.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics. Per the preregistered contract, exactly one initial model-generation call was produced per intent and that same generated candidate was reused for both episodes (baseline and guarded). No independent first-pass generation per condition was performed; only downstream validation and the allowed repair could change the paired outcome. Adapter-level provider accounting records stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1} and hosted_model_call_event_count = 251, consistent with the shared_initial_candidate design.

Task bank and constraints. A deterministic task generator produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (e.g., make-before-break, all-down-before-change, protected interfaces). Tasks were labeled medium/hard/very_hard to exercise dependency and ordering constraints; full task manifest and representative payloads are archived in the evidence bundle.

Model, validator, and repair policy. All initial generations used the declared model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). The guarded pipeline submitted the shared candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5, which performs full_intent_constraint_validation: parsing CLI sequences, checking required_sequence ordering and workflow constraints, computing final_state snapshots, and producing a boolean valid flag and violation codes. When valid = false the pipeline permitted one automated template-driven repair (syntactic/order fixes only) and re-submitted the repaired candidate once. No multi-iteration repair or human escalation was allowed in the confirmatory policy.

Inclusion, contamination, and analysis. The preregistered exclusion rules remove items that prevent deterministic verification (vendor-parser failures) or contain credential-like tokens/denylist hits. Contamination detectors flag instruction-like embedded tokens; flagged items are excluded from primary analysis and handled in sensitivity analyses. The confirmatory primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 (exact McNemar two-sided) and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI computed with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). All execution and analysis artifacts are archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The adapter recorded planned_episode_count = 500 and completed_episode_count = 500 (250 pairs × 2 episodes). Provider-call audit reconciles hosted_model_call_event_count = 251 (250 shared initial generations + 1 repair) and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}.

Primary binary outcomes. Deterministic validator scoring produced baseline_success_count = 249/250 (0.996) and guarded_success_count = 250/250 (1.000). The paired contingency table is n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (guarded × baseline). The single discordant pair corresponds to the only exercised repair and thus the repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition is 1/250 = 0.4%.

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided on the discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) yields p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for guarded − baseline (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (i.e., 0 – 1.2 percentage points). These analysis artifacts (contingency CSV, condition summary, analysis log) are archived and referenced in the evidence bundle.

Representative validator diagnostics. Passed episodes show parsed_command_count equal to required_command_count from the task payload (examples: task-000003 parsed_command_count = 6 required_command_count = 6). No contamination flags or deterministic parser failures appeared in the confirmatory partition; missingness summary reports complete_pairs = 250 and all other missingness counts = 0.

Repair exercise. Only one automated repair was needed and it converted the sole failing baseline candidate to a guarded pass; the repair trace is archived.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation task bank, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single template-driven repair was small: the initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the guarded pipeline converted the sole failing candidate via the single permitted repair. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) bounds the maximum plausible verifier-detected improvement under these conditions.

Why the effect is small (artifact-grounded). First, the deterministic task generator encoded constrained intents and allowed_touched_fields that reduced instruction ambiguity. Second, the declared model produced highly consistent, syntactically well-formed sequences for these constrained intents. Third, the deterministic validator checks mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, final-state snapshot) and does not capture broader behavioral correctness in live protocol execution or complex emergent interactions.

Power, assumptions, and limits of inference. The preregistration power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 when selecting N_pairs = 250 to detect a 15 percentage-point absolute effect with ≈80% power. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) exceeds that assumption, reducing the run's power to detect small absolute improvements; consequently the paired-bootstrap CI is the practically informative summary. Crucially, the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed — the confirmatory estimand reported here applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition.

Threats to validity. Internal validity depends on prompt templates, the single-repair policy, and shared_initial_candidate semantics. Construct validity: the deterministic validator measures mechanically verifiable correctness but not live protocol-level correctness. External validity: the run used one model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation on a synthetic partition; multi-model, production-scale, adversarial, or vendor-heterogeneous evidence is not provided by this confirmatory run.

Implications. These artifact-grounded results suggest that in tightly constrained emulation-style tasks with a capable LLM the marginal verifier-detected improvement from a single repair may be small. This does not imply validators and repairs are unnecessary in broader operational contexts; richer validators, additional repair iterations, human escalation, production heterogeneity, or adversarial threats could materially change the benefit calculus.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to quantify the marginal verifier-detected effect of deterministic validation plus a single automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks (gpt-5-mini), initial candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). The preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed; broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All referenced execution and analysis artifacts are archived and discoverable via the evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Autonomy and human role: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, model prompting, model calls, deterministic validation, the single permitted repair, analysis, drafting, peer-review, and revision without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and framework: declared model used for initial generations = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses). Deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The guarded pipeline permitted at most one automated, template-driven repair per episode as specified in the preregistration.

Preregistration and immutable prompt reference: preregistered study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the archived manifest). Immutable master prompt initiating the autonomous run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. The full execution and analysis evidence bundle (execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis artifacts) is archived and discoverable via the project evidence manifest referenced in the submission materials (single manifest pointer included there); the Disclosure here omits per-file path-level bookkeeping to preserve concise, publication-facing disclosure.

Executed estimand and deviation disclosure: The preregistration included multiple partitions (synthetic/emulation, community, production-like) and a preregistered sim-to-real confirmatory contrast. Deviation disclosure: the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed in this run; the executed confirmatory estimand reported in this paper is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only (N_pairs = 250; shared_initial_candidate semantics). Provider-call accounting reconciles to model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation + 1 repair) and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1} as recorded in the archived deterministic reconciliation artifact.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax and prescribed workflow sequences) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent cross-device interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
